long_biography.plain_text:
After working as a shipbroker, Kondylis moved from arranging transactions to controlling shipping companies and their commercial employment. By the mid-2010s, Larus was expanding through dry-bulk purchases and newbuildings, while associated tanker interests broadened his exposure. His Kondinave platform developed alongside that fleet, combining chartering, sale-and-purchase advice, operations and investment analysis from Piraeus.

Today Kondinave markets a mixed fleet and seeks voyage, trip, time or bareboat employment as market conditions change. Larus remains a substantial dry-bulk manager, with ships trading internationally under separate technical-management arrangements. Kondylis is still identified as managing director of Kondinave and a senior figure at Larus. His earlier brokerage experience now anchors an owner-operator model built around commercial management and asset selection.

uncertainties: Identity is resolved at 93 rather than very high. The authoritative record supplies the exact Alexios Kondylis-to-Allure A relationship, while the Hellenic Shipbrokers Association, Kondinave, Dun & Bradstreet, ClassNK, the Swedish Club, TradeWinds and Greek reporting independently converge on Alexios/Alexis Kondylis, Kondinave, Larus, Piraeus and Greek shipping. Public yacht sources confirm Allure A's exact 1994 build and Greek operating context but do not publish the private owner.

Alexios and Alexis are treated as English variants for the same Greek given name. The Hellenic Shipbrokers Association and Dun & Bradstreet use Alexios with Kondinave's exact address, while Kondinave, ClassNK and shipping coverage use Alexis. The Samos civil engineer and a refrigeration-business namesake have different companies, geographies and middle-name patterns and are excluded.

Dun & Bradstreet gives the principal's full name as Alexios Emmanouil Kondylis. A second strong source does not establish whether Emmanouil is a conventional middle name or a Greek patronymic, so middle_names and corresponding sort-field changes remain unproposed.

The authoritative relationship begins in 1994, matching Allure A's public build year. That timing and the vessel's Greek operating context strengthen the bridge but do not establish whether Kondylis commissioned, acquired or later restructured ownership of the yacht; none of those mechanisms is asserted.

The authoritative input records Allure A at 41 metres and 221 GT. Public sources agree on approximately 41 metres but commonly report 245 GT, while an older vessel profile reports 221 GT. The discrepancy likely reflects source or measurement changes and is excluded from the biographies.

Kondinave's official site says it markets and commercially manages a mixed fleet; it does not say Kondylis personally owns every listed ship. TradeWinds and Greek reporting support his control of Larus and tanker interests, but company-level vessels and transaction prices are not converted into personal assets or net worth.

A family-linked property company formed in 2025 through Larus Cyprus involves Kondylis' adult children. That corporate action does not show that property is a principal personal wealth sector for Alexios Kondylis, and the relatives' assets and roles are not imported into his biography or classifications.

Shipping & Maritime is independently supported for both original wealth creation and current primary industry. The broker-to-controller record, dry-bulk fleet, tanker interests and continuing commercial-management role leave no comparably evidenced non-maritime sector.

Self-made is used rather than either starting-position subtype. TradeWinds documents the move from shipbroker to fleet controller, and no inheritance is reported, but reliable sources do not disclose enough family, capital or launch history to decide whether his start was independent or advantaged.

Operator is more precise than Founder because sources document control, directorship and managing-director work but do not clearly establish who founded Kondinave or Larus. The founder_operator calibration describes the narrative style only and does not override the formal Operator classification.

Ship chartering is the only minimum-useful approved tag because Kondinave documents a repeated, defining charter-employment model under Kondylis' leadership. Shipbroking is excluded because sources establish a former career and association membership but not its duration or independent material contribution to wealth. Tanker shipping is excluded because the evidence for current control is less complete than for the predominantly dry-bulk platform.

No reliable public source establishes a birth date, exact birthplace, secondary nationality, secondary residence or collision-safe personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website. The official Kondinave site is proposed as Company Website.

Forbes-first searches found no dedicated profile or reliably attributable article. Allure A and all yacht, charter, crew, location and specification material are excluded from the biographies, which remain source-invisible and family-asset conscious.
